Title: ProductPoints — Priority resolution / no-stacking: ALL(pri=80) beats PRIORITY(pri=70) on shared SKU; QA-LOY-PRIO-001 earns ALL factor not PRIORITY factor
Section: Loyalty > Product Points Loyalty > Earning > Priority Resolution
Preconditions: Runner-native (cart oracle). ORG_USER is in no specific group — ALL(pri=80) wins for both LT-001 and QA-LOY-PRIO-001. ALL defines factor=500 for BOTH SKUs. PRIORITY(pri=70) defines factor=999 for QA-LOY-PRIO-001 but does NOT win (lower priority). The discriminating assertion: AMT_PRIO001 × price_LT001 = AMT_LT001 × price_PRIO001 (cross-multiplication proves both are earning at the SAME factor=500 from the SAME winning program ALL). If PRIORITY had won/stacked, AMT_PRIO001 × price_LT001 would be != AMT_LT001 × price_PRIO001. Fixed fixtures — no per-test mutation needed.

PRIORITY(pri=70) defines factor=999 for QA-LOY-PRIO-001 but does NOT win (lower priority number 70 < 80; single winner takes all; no stacking). This cross-multiplication proves both SKUs resolved to the same factor from the same single winning program (ALL). Note: the runner cannot execute arithmetic cross-path assertions inline; the [EVIDENCE] block documents the mathematical discriminant for human review; the structural gate (both > 0, correct currency) is the automated signal.
